section_title: 4.3. Agroforestry Model: Aonla based Agri-horticultural System
summary: This document describes the Aonla (Phyllanthus emblica) based agri-horticultural system, an agroforestry model adopted in the Bundelkhand region of India. It details the tree's habitat, phenology, propagation, cultural operations, and economic benefits, noting its profitability in poor and marginal lands.

heading_path: 4.3. Agroforestry Model: Aonla based Agri-horticultural System
passages.text: Aonla starts fruiting after 4 years of plantation and can give 400 to 500 kg/ha fruits and gradually the fruit yield increases with increasing age of trees. At the age of 10 years, it can yield up to 120 kg fruits per plant. After seven years of Aonla based agri-horticulture system (Aonla+ green gram/black gram), the B:C ratio of the system was 1.84. However, it increased to 3.28 at the age of 13 years of the system.

heading_path: 4.3. Agroforestry Model: Aonla based Agri-horticultural System
passages.text: The Aonla based agri-horticulture system has been proven to be one of the most profitable agroforestry systems in poor and marginal lands of drought-prone Bundelkhand region. It helps farmers to earn profits even in conditions of crop failure due to weather vagaries (Newaj et al. 2006).
